Then reason: The question stem states that A is the intersection point of any two meridian circles, so A is a pole; in the diagram, B is below A and is tangent to the 52°S latitude circle, indicating that A should be the South Pole. The difference from the South Pole to 52°S is 38°, while from O as the center to the great-circle boundary B is 90°, so O to the South Pole is about 52°, that is, O is roughly located near 38°S. Also because the dates on the east and west sides of point B are different and the global ranges of the old and new dates are equal, it can be judged that the relevant date boundary line differs from the date line by 180°; combined with O and B in the diagram being located on two sides of the South Pole, O roughly falls in the Southern Hemisphere, close to a region where ocean is dominant. Therefore, the prominent geographical feature of the hemisphere centered on point O is that the ocean area is vast.
